lesson_title: The Battery Lie: Nothing Ever Runs Out of Charge
hook_text: Your flat battery still has ALL its charge. So what actually ran out?
clip_script: Your phone dies and you say the battery is out of charge. Here is the thing — it is not. Every coulomb of charge that was ever in that circuit is still there. Charge just circulates: out of the positive terminal, through the phone, back into the negative terminal, around and around, never used up. Think of supporters streaming through a stadium gate — the people are never consumed; it is their ticket money that gets spent. Charge is the people. Energy is the money. The battery is not a charge tank, it is a pump: its chemistry loads energy onto every coulomb that passes through — 1,5 joules per coulomb for a small cell, 12 for a car battery. That is all a volt is: joules per coulomb. The screen and the speaker spend that energy, the coulombs come home empty, and the pump loads them again — until the chemicals inside are finished reacting. THAT is what ran out: chemical energy, not charge. Say it in the exam and it is free marks: charge is conserved; the battery's energy is spent.
visual_style: A glowing circuit drawn as a stadium concourse: charge as a crowd circulating through gates, energy as bright coins loaded onto each person by a pump-shaped battery, coins spent at a lightbulb turnstile that blazes brighter with each payment.
pacing: Bold claim up front, quick crowd-and-coins build, snap landing on the exam sentence.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never call it 'out of charge' again.
